chunks: And it is narrated from a man of Thaqif that he said:

ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام appointed me over Bāniqyā and a district from the Sawād of al-Kūfah. He said to me, while the people were present: “Examine your land revenue, be diligent in it, and do not leave even a dirham of it. Then when you want to proceed to your post, pass by me.”

He said: So I came to him, and he said to me: “What you heard from me was a stratagem. Beware lest you strike a Muslim, or a Jew, or a Christian over a dirham of kharaj, or sell a working animal for a dirham. Indeed, we have been commanded to take from it what is surplus/easy.”

key_terms.الْعَفْوَ: what is easy, surplus, or reasonably taken without hardship
key_terms.خَرَاجَكَ: your land revenue or tax assessment to be collected
key_terms.خُدْعَةٌ: a strategic statement not intended as the final operative instruction
key_terms.دَابَّةَ عَمَلٍ: a working animal used for livelihood, which must not be seized unjustly
key_terms.مُسْلِمًا: a Muslim subject who must not be wronged in collection
key_terms.نَصْرَانِيًّا: a Christian subject under governance who must not be mistreated
key_terms.يَهُودِيًّا: a Jewish subject under governance who must not be mistreated

ai.seo_question: How did Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام instruct officials to collect kharaj without oppression?
ai.summary: This hadith shows Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام instructing a tax official not to oppress people in the collection of kharaj. It emphasizes justice, restraint, and mercy in governance, including fair treatment of Muslims and protected non-Muslims alike.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1605 - It is narrated from a man of Thaqif who said:

"Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) appointed me over Banqiya and a portion of the lands of Kufa. He said to me, in the presence of the people: 'Inspect your revenue and be diligent in collecting it; do not leave even a single dirham. When you are ready to head to your assignment, come see me.'

I went to him, and Imam (as) said to me: 'What you heard from me was a strategy. Be cautious not to strike a Muslim, a Jew, or a Christian for a dirham of revenue, nor to seize a working animal for a dirham. We have been commanded to take only what is easy for them to give.'"
